messages:
anya: Heads-up — we should lock down when GPU alerts page vs when they just create tickets. Operator fatigue last week was rough. Any objections to a short concrete proposal?

mike.h: +1 to standardizing. can you sketch the proposal?

anya: Rough idea: three buckets — transient noise (ticket), sustained degradation (page), and catastrophic (page + broadcast). Use duration + cardinality + error-class. Example heuristics: p95 latency spike > 2x baseline for > 3m AND affected nodes > 5 => page. single-node OOM spike => ticket unless it's repeating (3x in 30m).

cassie: I like duration+cardinality. also add region-awareness: if an alert hits a single region with >20% capacity impact => page even if duration short.

derek: Cheap win: add a 90s debounce on alerts that are purely CPU/GPU usage with normal nvtop churn. avoids stomping on short scheduling spikes.

mike.h: Can we codify into Prometheus rules? proposed alert expr for the sustained case:```expr
(sum by(cluster) (rate(gpu_inference_latency_seconds_bucket{le=\"0.5\"}[5m])) /
(sum by(cluster) (rate(gpu_inference_latency_seconds_count[5m]))) > 2
```then add for >3m and node_count>5. (pseudo)

anya: + example for OOM bursts:```expr
increase(gpu_memory_ooms_total[30m]) >= 3
``` -> ticket creation. if increase(...) >= 5 within 30m -> page.

cassie: What about grouping? we should group by deployment and region so a single flaring workload doesn't page every pager. group_key = (deployment, region).

sre-bot: Reminder: current paging volume last week: 72 pages, 48% were single-node transient. Link: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/ops/gpu-pages?orgId=1

derek: Also note cost angle — too many pages lead to on-call overtime. If we change thresholds we should run an A/B for 2 weeks and monitor missed-severity regression via SLOs.

anya: Actionable plan: 1) implement duration debounce (90s) for usage-only alerts 2) add cardinality threshold (node_count>5) for pages 3) region-capacity override (>=20% impact) 4) group_by=(deployment,region) 5) run A/B test on half clusters for 14 days and compare page rate + SLO errors.

mike.h: I'm happy to PR rule changes. will add tests and a canary on staging clusters first.

cassie: I'll update the runbook with the new thresholds and add examples for first responder triage.

anya: pinging @derek for oncall handoff adjustments and @mike.h once PR is open. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Deploy bot: rule-change-pr-546 merged to staging at 1732112000.

mike.h: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/repo/infra/alerts/pull/546 — contains prometheus rules + alertmanager grouping. please review.

derek: noted. i'll update the oncall rota and mute windows doc (ops/oncall/mute-windows.md) after we confirm canary metrics.

anya: Closing note: keep an eye on network egress alerts too — sometimes a noisy network equals gpu flares and we shouldn't page twice. if network-related, prefer ticket + correlation tag.

cassie: Agreed — add label correlated_with=network when the net metric is > threshold.

mike.h: I'll include that label in the alerts.

anya: cool. end of thread.
